narrative.overview: Sayloom feels like a carefully prepared working sheet: warm paper, exact rules, ink-led typography, and a blue thread that connects source, transformation, outgoing state, and safe recovery detail. It is a quiet macOS utility rather than a generic dashboard. The interface should disappear during repeated use while remaining legible enough to trust at a glance. This is an extension of the incumbent code-defined world, not a replacement. New setup surfaces and inspectable failures inherit the same paper, rule, rail, heading, field, and control language.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper and cool output surfaces bounded by fine, functional rules.
Near-black utility chrome with one restrained thread-blue accent.
Editorial serif for identity and working text; workhorse sans for controls.
Vertically ordered, spacious task canvases with compact operational metadata.
State is always written in words; color supports meaning but never carries it.
Failures remain inspectable as quiet, ruled records beside their owning workflow without interrupting raw fail-open.

rules.name: The Blue Thread Rule
rules.body: Blue appears only where the interface needs to show selection, action, focus, or live state. Large inactive regions remain neutral.

rules.name: The Written State Rule
rules.body: Waiting, stale, failed, disabled, installed, and selected states must have adjacent text. Never ask hue alone to explain state.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif identifies the brand, titles the working sheet, and carries authored or generated prose. Sans-serif operates the product.

rules.name: The Compact Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracking is reserved for short labels; never apply it to paragraphs, long actions, or wrapped navigation text.

rules.name: The Linear Proof Rule
rules.body: Original → transformation context → Cleaned → Outgoing must read in that order without crossing the page or opening a manager.

rules.name: The Sheet, Not Card Rule
rules.body: Borders organize working surfaces; shadows only separate a complete sheet from the page. Do not turn every group into a card.

rules.name: The Earned Curve Rule
rules.body: A curve must identify a switch, a compact state, or a circular action. Content containers remain sheet-like.

rules.name: The Inspectable Failure Rule
rules.body: Every API failure leaves a durable, safe, copyable explanation at its owning workflow while the user's available path continues independently.

dos: Do inherit the incumbent paper, rail, rule, type, and control language on Workspace, Cleanup, and Targets.
Do preserve generous text canvases and compact setup controls.
Do keep prompt and vocabulary context visible with Cleaned.
Do keep Original, Cleaned, and Outgoing source unambiguous in every state.
Do use one continuous sheet or ruled list before adding another container.
Do preserve keyboard focus, resizing, text selection, and readable wrapping.
Do keep each simultaneous API failure separately named, persistent, and expandable at the workflow that owns it.
Do make visible safe details and copied details the same bounded dataset.
donts: Don't introduce rounded dashboard cards, bento grids, glass, or a second accent identity.
Don't use serif type for buttons, form labels, navigation, or status text.
Don't decorate inactive regions with blue or rely on color-only state.
Don't place Original and Cleaned side by side or hide the resizable divider.
Don't add recording-review UI, a target picker, or delivery claims to the workspace visual world.
Don't persist or depict real dictated content in documentation or comps.
Don't use a toast as the only failure record or collapse unrelated errors into one global banner.
Don't let an expanded error disclosure block editing, choosing Original, or understanding the current outgoing value.
